- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". content.text: Let me confirm the method name this lives in.

h01.

**S3 presign runner** (`s3presign.Runner`) — keeps S3 presigned attachment URLs from expiring by re-presigning them. It runs **every 12 hours** (the `runnerInterval` constant at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`), and also performs an immediate run-once on startup.

It is wired into server startup in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`, which is called from `Server.Start` at **`server/server.go:129`**. The runner is created and kicked off at lines 162–171 of that same file.

**Component** — `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`)
**Schedule** — every 12 hours (`runnerInterval`, line 27)
**Wiring site** — `server/server.go:129` (`s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` called from `Start`; runner instantiated at line 162)
